text: Our ability to respond to danger. <break time="0.8s" /> Has been important for survival. <break time="0.8s" /> So feeling worried in uncertain situations. <break time="0.8s" /> Is normal. <break time="0.8s" /> Feelings of worry. <break time="0.8s" /> Which are activated in anticipation of future events. <break time="0.8s" /> Are often experienced. <break time="0.8s" /> In everyday situations. <break time="0.8s" /> For example. <break time="0.8s" /> We may feel nervous. <break time="0.8s" /> Imagining unlikely events. <break time="0.8s" /> Such as a computer crashing during an important presentation. <break time="0.8s" /> To some extent. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking through potential scenarios. <break time="0.8s" /> Can be helpful. <break time="0.8s" /> When our worries exceed our control. <break time="0.8s" /> However they cause us unnecessary suffering. <break time="0.8s" /> Consider how many times you have lost sleep. <break time="0.8s" /> Thinking about a terrible situation. <break time="0.8s" /> Which, in the end. <break time="0.8s" /> Did not actually take place. <break time="0.8s" /> If that situation actually occurred. <break time="0.8s" /> It only goes to show. <break time="0.8s" /> That worrying about it. <break time="0.8s" /> Did nothing to prevent it from happening. <break time="0.8s" /> It is worth making a conscious effort. <break time="0.8s" /> Then to stop worrying endlessly about events you may not experience.
